meta.title: FAQ · Amplio
meta.description: Plain answers for brands and creators on Amplio: pricing, tracking, payments and the demo data.

hero.title: Questions, answered.
hero.sub: The short answers, for brands and for creators.

items.q: How do you tie a sign-up to a post?
items.a: Each collaboration gets its own tracked link, and every click on it is stored with the time and the source. A small pixel on your site then ties each sign-up back to that click, so you see the post and the creator behind it.
€0 per month. No subscription, no retainer. You pay each creator's fixed price for each post that gets published, and never per click or per view.

items.q: How do I pick a creator?
items.a: Creators are ranked by a fit score against your ideal customer. Each card shows the creator's headline, industries, price and audience figures.

items.q: Do I see the post before it goes live?
items.a: Yes. You send an offer and write the brief, the creator writes a draft, and it only goes live after you approve it.

items.q: When do I pay, and how?
items.a: You keep a wallet. Once a post is live, you pay for it from there and a ledger row is written. In this build, card top-ups are Stripe stubs: the flow is shown, but no real money moves.

items.q: Are the numbers on this site real?
items.a: The public numbers come from a seeded demo workspace. They show what tracking looks like, not results from real customers.

items.q: Does it cost anything to join?
items.a: No. Joining is free, and there's no exclusivity: you can work with any brand, on Amplio or anywhere else.

items.q: How do I set my price?
items.a: You set one fixed price per post, from €20. Brands pay that price for each published post, never per click or per view.
Several posts sold together at a package price. You can offer up to 3 bundles next to your price per post.

items.q: Do I have to accept every offer?
items.a: No. You accept the offers you like and leave the rest.
When a brand pays for your live post, a ledger row is written and the payment shows up in your earnings. In this build, bank payouts are Stripe stubs: the flow is shown, but no real money moves.

items.q: What does the LinkedIn import do?
items.a: It reads your public LinkedIn profile to fill in your card. If it can't read the profile, you enter the details by hand.

meta.title: Privacy · Amplio
meta.description: What Amplio stores, why, and how to delete it.

privacy.title: Privacy Notice
privacy.sub: What Amplio stores, why, and how to delete it. This is a demonstration build, so the short answer is: not much, and none of it leaves the database.

sections.title: What we store
paragraphs: Your account: your email, your name, a hash of your password and a session cookie.
Your workspace: the campaigns, briefs, collaborations, messages and ledger rows you create.
Newsletter sign-ups: emails entered in the earlier version's newsletter form are stored and nothing else. The form is no longer on the site, and no email is sent in this build.

sections.title: What tracking stores
paragraphs: When someone clicks a tracked link, we store a hashed IP address, the browser's user agent, the referring page and a click id.
The pixel on a brand's site sends events such as a sign-up or a purchase. We store each one with the click id it belongs to.

sections.title: Cookies
paragraphs: We set one first-party session cookie when you sign in. It is httpOnly, so scripts on the page can't read it.
When a tracked link redirects, we set a first-party click cookie so a later sign-up can be tied back to that click.
There are no advertising, analytics or third-party cookies.

The tracking pixel keeps the click id and a random visitor id in the browser's local storage on any site that installs it (in this build, our demo landing page), so a later sign-up can be tied back to the click.

sections.title: Deleting your data
paragraphs: Go to Settings → Delete account. Your user, your workspace and everything attached to them are removed in one go.
Demo accounts can't be deleted, because everyone shares them.

meta.title: Terms · Amplio
meta.description: The plain terms for using Amplio, a demonstration build where no real money moves.

terms.title: Terms & Policies
terms.sub: Amplio is a working rebuild made for demonstration. Using it means agreeing to a few plain things.

sections.title: This is a demonstration
paragraphs: The creators, posts and results in the demo accounts are seeded sample data.
The database can be reseeded at any time, which resets the data. Don't store anything you need to keep.

sections.title: No real money moves
paragraphs: Wallet balances, payouts and withdrawals are ledger rows, not payments. Card top-ups and bank payouts are Stripe stubs: the flow is shown, but nothing is charged and nothing is paid out.

sections.title: Your content
paragraphs: You are responsible for what you post: briefs, drafts, messages and links.
Only use tracked links and the pixel on sites you control.

sections.title: The numbers you see
paragraphs: The numbers on the public pages come from a seeded demo workspace, not from real customers.
